standard_prerequisites.name: Integrality of the invariant subring extension, via the monic polynomial which is the product over the group of the conjugates
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the integrality input on which the no-inclusion criterion is applied.

standard_prerequisites.name: The absence of inclusion relations among primes over a given prime in an integral extension
standard_prerequisites.use: Locates the primes over p so that conjugacy is the only remaining question.

standard_prerequisites.name: Prime avoidance
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element x used to build the invariant y.

core_obligations: Observe that R^G in R is integral, since every x in R is a root of the monic polynomial prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(x)) with coefficients in R^G[T] (proof lines 32687-32688).
Conclude from the no-inclusion criterion for integral extensions that there are no inclusion relations among the primes lying over a given prime p (proof lines 32689-32691).
Assume the lemma fails and choose, by prime avoidance, an element x in q' with x not in sigma(q) for all sigma in G (proof lines 32692-32694).
Form y = prod_{sigma in G} sigma(x), note that y lies in R^G and in p = R^G cap q' (proof lines 32695-32696).
Observe that x not in sigma(q) for all sigma means sigma(x) not in q for all sigma, so y is not in q because q is a prime ideal (proof lines 32697-32699).
Conclude the contradiction using y in p contained in q, which proves the transitivity assertion (proof lines 32699-32700).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite group G acting on a ring R and asserts that any two primes q and q' of R lying over the same prime of the invariant subring R^G are conjugate under the action of G (source lines 32679-32684). The proof first observes that the extension R^G in R is integral, because every x in R is a root of the monic polynomial prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(x)) with coefficients in R^G[T]; consequently there are no inclusion relations among the primes lying over a given prime p, by the no-inclusion criterion for integral extensions (proof lines 32687-32691). The argument is then by contradiction and is the substantive part: if the lemma fails one can choose x in q' with x not in sigma(q) for every sigma in G, by the prime avoidance lemma; then y = prod_{sigma in G} sigma(x) lies in R^G and in p = R^G cap q', while the condition x not in sigma(q) for all sigma means sigma(x) not in q for all sigma, so y is not in q because q is prime — contradicting y in p contained in q (proof lines 32692-32700). The non-routine content is the construction of the invariant element y and the use of primality to place it on both sides of the contradiction.
